### Is a signal detecting damage, or just uncertainty?


**0.5b_v2**

| signal | AUC (flip) | rho with damage | rho with damage, within budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| top1-top2 margin | 0.877 | 0.382 | 0.214 |
| eviction consensus | 0.808 | 0.955 | 0.819 |
| est dropped mass (mean) | 0.807 | 0.946 | 0.785 |
| est dropped mass (max) | 0.807 | 0.921 | 0.620 |
| fully-dropped mass | 0.802 | 0.931 | 0.703 |
| cross-layer dropped-mass std | 0.796 | 0.916 | 0.571 |
| sparse attn entropy | 0.409 | 0.189 | 0.111 |

A signal with a high AUC but a near-zero damage correlation is an uncertainty detector, not a fidelity signal: it fires on steps that would flip under any perturbation and stays quiet on confidently wrong steps, which is the case that matters.


### H4 — does divergence predict end-task wrongness?

| run | dense acc | answerable | rho (all) | rho (answerable) | rho (within budget) | AUC answerable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5b_v2 | 0.458 | 165/360 | -0.435 | -0.870 | -0.821 | 0.936 |

Falsification threshold: |rho| < 0.5 kills H4. 'All' pools requests the dense model already fails, where sparse cannot degrade anything; 'within budget' rules out budget acting as a common cause.

Measured probe/step cost ratio r = 0.55 (paired-step ratio (UNDERSTATES r)). H2 falsification: a +/-5% bound costing >15% throughput.
Short-trace verdict: **INCONCLUSIVE**.
Scale-free / primary verdict: **NOT FALSIFIED at stream length >= 10000 steps (valid estimators only: fixed + Hoeffding, fixed + EmpBernstein)**.
Coverage-valid estimators: ['fixed + Hoeffding', 'fixed + EmpBernstein']; best valid: fixed + EmpBernstein.

### Probes needed for target width (scale-free, valid estimators)

| estimator | w=0.2 | w=0.1 | w=0.05 |
|---|---|---|---|
| fixed + Hoeffding | 875 | 4075 | 18700 |
| fixed + EmpBernstein | 225 | 1050 | 5325 |
| fixed + Betting | 125 | 487 | 2312 |

Width scaling exponent beta = 0.427 (width ~ p^-beta; 0.5 is the sqrt-n rate, so cost grows superlinearly in guarantee strength).
